A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. Content can be matched despite substantial reformatting; v2 adds Appendix K and a conference checklist.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix J report original RNN, Langevin-dynamics and chaotic-observer experiments, including convergence measurements and GPU runtimes.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix J retain original simulation results and report revised numerical plots alongside convergence and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The merit objective, DEER/Gauss-Newton updates, parallel scan, observer construction and contractive SSM parameterization in Appendix I are retained. The added LLE discussion does not introduce a different trajectory-evaluation method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate mean-field RNNs, Langevin dynamics in a two-well potential, and the same nine dysts chaotic systems with stable observers. Sequence-length adjustments remain within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 6 retains DEER, quasi-DEER, gradient descent and sequential evaluation, with sequential evaluation included in the timing comparison. Additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Figures 2(right), 5 and 6 change the reported RNN length from 954 to 1000. Appendix J.3 replaces total-loss tolerances of 0.1 and 10^-7 with per-step L/T tolerances of 10^-4 and 10^-10; the first is equivalent to total loss 0.1 at T=1000. Langevin LLE reporting also changes to continuous-time units. These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The g-to-LLE sensitivity curve in Figure 4 and the error/convergence diagnostics in Figures 5 and 7 contain revised evidence. Figure 5's chaotic-divergence case is now reported at T=1000. The analytical questions and qualitative conclusions remain the same.

E5.justification: Both retain 20-seed summaries and min-max ranges, five seeds with five timing repetitions in Figure 6, and averaging over three initial vectors for LLE estimation. The new checklist restates existing statistical reporting rather than documenting increased replication.

E6.justification: RNN convergence curves and timing points are updated under the revised reported settings. Figure 3's LLE changes from -0.015 to -1.45 alongside the new time-normalization explanation; this does not establish more stable dynamics. Table 1's numerical values and the main qualitative findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix K introduces continuous-time variational equations, an LLE definition and a derivation relating Euler discretization to LLE normalization. The core conditioning and DEER convergence theorems, assumptions and proofs are substantively retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the predictability-conditioning connection, DEER convergence contributions and O((log T)^2) parallel-evaluation claim under the stated conditions. The revised evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The conclusion removes the discussion of weighted merit functions as potential preconditioners. Appendix K newly explains the dependence of LLE magnitude on time normalization and preservation of its sign. Existing memory and finite-precision limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-code link and code/documentation access statements. Appendix J.3 newly discloses batch size 1, while Appendix K explicitly describes Euler discretization and LLE reporting conventions. These additions improve documentation without establishing corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: References expand to include additional recurrent-reasoning, stable-RNN, stochastic-differential-equation and LLE literature; Song et al. (2021) and the ARC Prize blog reference are removed. Section 6 specifies quasi-DEER where v1 described Farsang et al.'s method as DEER. The central novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits and condensation, updates author information and citation style, and adds Appendix K and the NeurIPS checklist. The main section order and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: The manuscript undergoes a comprehensive conversion to NeurIPS formatting, changing the title block, typography, margins, text density and figure/table placement throughout. Existing figures are resized and partly redrawn, with revised captions and axes, including Figure 7's LLE scale.

improvement.justification: The code-access information, batch-size disclosure and explicit reporting conventions address documentation gaps and modestly improve reproducibility and interpretation. The gains are limited by removal of the weighted-norm discussion and Appendix K's finite-step LLE equality, which omits the limiting qualification used in its derivation. The central scientific contribution and empirical conclusions remain stable.
